source.title: Emergent Misalignment via In-Context Learning: Narrow in-context examples can produce broadly misaligned LLMs
source.authors: N. Afonin; N. Andriyanov; Vahagn Hovhannisyan; Nikhil Bageshpura; Kyle Liu; Kevin Zhu; Sunishchal Dev; Ashwinee Panda; Oleg Y. Rogov; Elena Tutubalina; Alexander Panchenko; Mikhail Seleznyov

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether narrow in-context examples produce broad misalignment, using inference-time prompting rather than fine-tuning.
record.gate_note: The paper reports misalignment rates for in-context examples, no-context controls, example-type and mixture conditions, and priority-prompt conditions. The two-example demonstrations and reasoning-trace examples are qualitative, not separately rated outcomes. Figure 5 reports an example-count trend, but its per-count values are figure-only; it is omitted due to the 60-row cap. Table 10's category results and Figure 4's priority-prompt results are included.
record.test_reason: The study measures misaligned free-form answers to Betley et al.'s unrelated evaluation questions after narrow in-context examples, with no fine-tuning. It compares these against a zero-example control across 11 frontier models in four families. This bears directly on V3. It does not fine-tune, run RL or probe internals, so V1, V2, V4, V5 and V6 are untested. The rows measure ICL rates, not fine-tuned open models, so they do not bear on V7 either.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that narrow in-context examples, including non-harmful TruthfulQA falsehoods, elicit misaligned answers to benign unrelated questions across four families (1-24% at 16 shots, from 2 shots). They find EM grows with example count, larger models are typically more susceptible, and reasoning does not protect. Safety-priority prompts reduce EM and context-priority prompts increase it, which they read as a safety vs context-following conflict. The paraphrase omits that insecure-code examples elicited no EM in context.
record.recipe_differences: Uses inference-time in-context examples rather than fine-tuning or activation steering; it tests narrow misaligned and falsehood examples across frontier model families.
record.method_sensitivity: Rates differ by model, in-context dataset/category, fraction of incorrect examples, and priority instruction. The authors report increasing rates with example count; reasoning-mode comparisons were generally not statistically significant.

fits_no_version.finding: In reasoning traces of misaligned responses, 67% mention harm, dangerous or reckless; models recognise harm but follow the in-context pattern.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context EM reflects a conflict between safety training and context-following rather than changed harm perception.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger models show higher ICL EM in 5 of 9 size comparisons and lower in 1; thinking variants are marginally higher than non-thinking ones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ICL-induced EM does not decrease with model scale or explicit reasoning.

fits_no_version.finding: Inference-time 'Prioritize safety' and 'Prioritize adhering to context' prompts lower and raise EM respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time priority instructions modulate ICL-induced EM.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2025)
record.problems: The main evaluation uses GPT-4o as judge and filters responses with coherency below 50; the paper acknowledges judge robustness concerns. Human validation covers 136 Gemini-2.5-Pro outputs, not all models. Some per-model results are available only in figures. Exact sizes are unknown for closed-source models, and model coverage is limited to 11 models across four families. The authors also note that the one-turn setup and limited chain-of-thought sample may not generalize.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 5's separate 2–32 example-count sweep for Gemini-3-Pro and Kimi-K2-Thinking is omitted due to the 60-row cap; the text says rates increase with example count and EM appears with two examples. Figure 6 and Appendix C report no EM for insecure-code examples and are recorded in r59.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on insecure code and no secure/educational controls. Only insecure-code ICL (r59) is tested.
No fine-tuning on any narrow dataset; the bad-advice datasets are used only in context.
No representation or persona-feature analysis. Reasoning-trace word counts are not a test of a linear direction.
No training-time inoculation or benign re-training. Only inference-time priority prompts are tested.
No fine-tuned open models, so effect size after training, seed robustness of fine-tunes, coherence-filter sensitivity and training-time onset are all untested.

missing.what: 16-shot bad-advice EM rates for Gemini 2.5 Flash (0.099) and Gemini 2.5 Pro (0.115)
Reasoning on/off at 16-shot TruthfulQA: Grok-4.1 Fast 1.8% vs 4.5%, Gemini 3 Flash 12.8% vs 15.9%
Expanded 100-question benign evaluation set: Gemini-3-Pro EM 0.55-0.66
64-shot bad-advice rates for Gemini 2.5 and Qwen models (up to 0.17), alongside the insecure-code zeros

record.verdict_notes: V7 links were removed from all rows: V7 is about fine-tuned open models and training dynamics, while this study is purely ICL. Several rows duplicate others (r23/r28/r33/r38 duplicate r10/r14/r15/r12; r41/r44/r47/r50 duplicate r01/r05/r06/r03), so counts across rows overstate independent evidence. The recorded 'peer_reviewed: ACL 2025' is doubtful: the arXiv v4 is dated 2026 and cites 2026 work. The insecure-code null agrees with the original paper's GPT-4o ICL null.

versions.untested_parts: Tests insecure-code examples in context, not fine-tuning on insecure code for an unsuspecting user or the matched secure-code and class-requested controls.
No fine-tuning on the other listed narrow datasets; the study tests in-context examples.
Does not test other models beyond those studied or multi-turn placement of examples; the paper notes all examples occur in the first user message.
No reinforcement learning or learned reward-hack intervention.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating the behavior.
Does not test training-time inoculation framing or brief benign retraining. It does test inference-time instructions to prioritize safety or context-following.

Examines rates across model families and some size comparisons, but does not test when the effect appears during training or sensitivity to the coherence filter. Open-model coverage is limited to the models reported.

relationships.display_finding: Sixteen bad-advice or falsehood examples, as well as conspiracy examples, produced misaligned-answer rates of 0.045 to 0.326, while the zero-example control gave essentially no misaligned answers.
